messages.content: The project manager approved the Sunday arrival. Before we commit, compare the three North Hills hotel options for all three nights, Sunday February 28 through Wednesday March 3. I need the actual stay totals, not just nightly rates.

I have three available options under the $235 pre-tax room limit. Using the quoted 13.25% combined lodging tax, the three-night totals are: AC Hotel Raleigh North Hills at $229 nightly: $687 room plus $91.03 tax, or $778.03. Its parking is another $18 nightly, so the total would be $832.03 with a car. Hampton Inn & Suites Raleigh Midtown at $205 nightly: $615 plus $81.49 tax, or $696.49; parking and breakfast are included. Courtyard Raleigh Midtown at $179 nightly: $537 plus $71.15 tax, or $608.15, with included parking. The Courtyard rate becomes nonrefundable seven days before arrival.
Are there any destination fees or other mandatory charges missing from those numbers?

No destination or resort fees are listed for any of the three rates. The totals include the room charge and lodging tax. Parking at the AC is optional rather than mandatory, so I showed it separately. The other two include parking at no additional charge. Incidental holds may appear temporarily at check-in, but they are not part of the final trip cost unless charged against.
I won't rent a car. Compare getting around from each one, especially in the morning. The workshop is at the North Hills client office.

The AC is the clear access leader: the client office is about a six-minute walk, so the morning trip has no fare and little traffic exposure. The Hampton is roughly 2.8 miles away; rides are currently estimated at 8-12 minutes in normal traffic and $12-$17 each way. The Courtyard is about 4.5 miles away; allow 12-18 minutes and approximately $15-$21 each way. Monday morning could run several minutes longer from either Midtown property.
Count all six workshop rides for the two Midtown hotels. Monday, Tuesday, and Wednesday, out and back each day.

For six local rides, the Hampton adds an estimated $72-$102, bringing lodging plus workshop transportation to $768.49-$798.49. The Courtyard adds about $90-$126, bringing that combined amount to $698.15-$734.15. The AC remains $778.03 because all six workshop transfers can be made on foot.
Wednesday isn't really a round trip. I check out in the morning, go to the workshop, then leave for RDU from the office after it ends.

You're right. That makes five hotel-office rides rather than six: two on Monday, two on Tuesday, and one Wednesday morning. Revised totals are $756.49-$781.49 for the Hampton and $683.15-$713.15 for the Courtyard, before the airport rides. The AC stays at $778.03 with the office walk.
Add the airport pieces too. Sunday from RDU to the hotel, then Wednesday from the client office to RDU. Is the second ride effectively the same regardless of hotel?

Yes. The Wednesday office-to-RDU ride is common to all three plans because you leave directly from North Hills. It is currently about 20-28 minutes and $29-$39. Sunday RDU-to-hotel is about $28-$36 to the AC, $27-$35 to the Hampton, and $30-$40 to the Courtyard. Estimated complete ground-inclusive totals are therefore: AC $835.03-$853.03; Hampton $812.49-$855.49; Courtyard $742.15-$792.15.
So the Hampton could end up costing essentially the same as the AC, depending on ride pricing.

Correct. At the low end, the Hampton is about $22.54 less. At the high end, it is about $2.46 more. Its included breakfast may reduce meal expense, but the hotel comparison itself is nearly a tie once the five workshop rides are included. The AC replaces those rides with short walks and gives a much more predictable total.
What are the cancellation deadlines? I don't want the cheap Courtyard rate to look better than it is if approval timing changes again.

The AC can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. local time on Saturday, February 27; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax, $259.34. The Hampton has the same 6:00 p.m. February 27 deadline and a one-night penalty of $232.16. The Courtyard remains cancelable until 11:59 p.m. local time on Sunday, February 21, then the entire $608.15 stay becomes nonrefundable.
Does the Hampton shuttle to North Hills?

No scheduled North Hills shuttle is included in this rate. The property lists only a limited local shuttle operating on weekday mornings, subject to availability, and the client office falls just outside its published service radius. I would not use it to reduce the transportation estimate.
Then compare the practical morning schedule. I need to be at the office by 8:15 Monday and 8:30 Tuesday and Wednesday.

From the AC, leaving at 8:05 Monday and around 8:20 Tuesday and Wednesday should cover the six-minute walk with a small margin. From the Hampton, I would request a ride by 7:45 Monday and 8:00 on the other mornings, allowing roughly 20-30 minutes for pickup, traffic, and entry. From the Courtyard, use 7:35 Monday and 7:50 Tuesday and Wednesday because both pickup time and the longer drive are less predictable.
The Courtyard saves real money, but losing the whole stay after February 21 is too much exposure. Between the other two, which one is strongest under the project rules?

The AC is the strongest overall. Its $229 nightly rate complies with the $235 pre-tax cap, and without a rental car the parking charge does not apply. Its estimated complete cost of $835.03-$853.03 overlaps the Hampton's $812.49-$855.49 range, while avoiding five rides, earlier morning departures, and surge-price uncertainty. The Hampton is defensible if included breakfast is valued separately, but it is not reliably cheaper after transportation.

Select the AC. Keep the no-car total separate from any incidental hold, and don't book the Courtyard as a backup. Can the room and the Sunday flight be held while I send the final combined amount back to the manager?

The AC is selected, and the Courtyard will not be held. The three-night hotel total is $778.03 with no parking charge; estimated airport transportation is $57-$75, making the hotel-and-ground total $835.03-$853.03. Combined with the $512 Sunday nonstop airfare, the working trip total is $1,347.03-$1,365.03, excluding meals and any temporary incidental authorization. Neither the hotel nor the flight currently offers a free hold at these quoted rates, so I have left both unbooked. The airfare, room availability, tax, and cancellation terms need to be rechecked when you give final approval.
